Fixture Bank Limited Partial — AI Readiness Gap Statement
What this statement assesses, and what it does not
PILLAR LEVEL ONLY. This is one pillar’s score and its five diagnostic questions. It is not a readiness assessment of any system,
model, dataset or use case, and it does not become one by being read alongside a use-case list assembled elsewhere.
NO USE CASES EXIST IN ANY DATASET HERE. The service ladder promises this statement "per candidate use case" and
P11’s own banking overlay names "AI readiness assessment per candidate banking use case" as an artefact — and not one
candidate use case is recorded anywhere in this workbench. Nothing below is per use case. Reading it as though it were would
give a use case a readiness verdict that was never assessed.
THE FOUR SCORES ARE NOT COMBINED. P11’s focus text names classification (P08), traceability (P07) and quality (P05) as
the dependencies AI rests on, so those three are printed beside it. No dataset defines a weighting across them, so no composite,
index or overall readiness score is computed. A single number here would be one nobody decided.
THREE STATES, AND THE DENOMINATOR IS PRINTED. A pillar with applicable questions and none answered reads NOT
ASSESSED — never 0, and it enters no mean. A pillar with no applicable questions under the active layer reads NOT
APPLICABLE. Unmeasured and low are different findings and this document never lets them print the same.

The five questions, and what was answered
Is there a register of certified reports and trusted datasets that consumers are directed to use?
Not answered. Contributes to neither the numerator nor the denominator.
Certification status is surfaced in consumption tools at the point of use.
Do AI and analytics use cases pass a data-readiness gate before development is approved?
Not answered. Contributes to neither the numerator nor the denominator.
Readiness is assessed automatically from catalogue, classification and quality metadata.
Are model and analytics inputs traceable to governed data elements?
Not answered. Contributes to neither the numerator nor the denominator.
Model drift is attributable to input data change, and input changes notify model owners automatically.
Is the content used to ground generative AI — documents, policies, customer records — classified and access-controlled before ingestion?
Not answered. Contributes to neither the numerator nor the denominator.
Ingestion is automatically gated on classification, with entitlement enforced at query time.

Does model risk management require evidenced data lineage for regulatory and credit models?
Not answered. Contributes to neither the numerator nor the denominator.
Lineage evidence is produced automatically from the governance platform for each validation cycle.

The dependency named in P11's own focus text: "Directly addresses the 2026 board question — GenAI cannot be deployed on data that cannot
be classified, traced or trusted, which makes governance the funded dependency of the AI budget."
Four numbers, four denominators, no fifth number. Which of the three dependencies matters most for a given deployment is a judgement about
that deployment, and this workbench holds no deployment to judge.

How the published frameworks reach this pillar
Each entry is one leaf dimension of one framework mapped onto this pillar, with the share of that dimension the pillar accounts for. The weight is
the share of the DIMENSION, not of the pillar — the pillar is not thereby covered to any percentage, and no coverage figure is given here.
Business intelligence is the consumption end of the data estate, which P11 measures.
Analytics management and P11 AI & Consumption address the same capability.
For a data programme, benefit is overwhelmingly realised at the consumption end, P11.
